scope: Neighborhood bakery site: daily menu from an API and pickup ordering
assumptions: Menu data uses a local fixture with adjustable delay; no real orders are submitted

system.authority: No existing system; derive tokens from the direction
system.tokenSource: DESIGN.md created from the selected direction before layout; code tokens in src/styles/tokens.css
system.expression: Warm craft without generic stock coziness
system.rationale: Lead with what was baked today and the pickup deadline

direction.concept: A chalkboard beside the till and a kraft paper bag: a handwritten daily menu where bake time matters more than slogans
direction.palette: Chalkboard graphite, kraft, and flour; one crust-colored accent for time and action; warm neutrals
direction.typography: Candidates: narrow-numeral sans, stencil display, handwritten accent. Choose a narrow sans for menu/time and handwriting only for notes such as Fresh at 7:40

references.source: Menu chalkboards in local bakeries (user-provided photos)
references.takeaway: Name, time, and price on one row with chalk annotations
Date stamp as a graphic motif
Tabular time presentation with tabular numerals

alternatives.premise: Typographic: daily menu board with bake times leads the first viewport
Image-led: a large dawn oven photograph, followed by the menu
Structural: the day's timeline from first bake to closing

signature: Baked at 7:40 stamp on each item
Chalk underline on hover and focus
direction.motion: Handcrafted but quick: chalk draws in, a stamp presses briefly without bouncing. Restrained tempo (micro 120, small 180, medium 260 ms), standard/enter/exit curves, non-overshooting springs. Signature detail: adding an item presses an In order stamp and rolls the order count. Reduced motion: chalk and stamp crossfade without movement

tasks.scenario: View today's menu and place a pickup order
tasks.outcome: The user sees an order number and pickup time
tasks.recovery: Menu loading failure shows a reason and retry; order failure preserves the selection

components.responsive: One column on phones, two on desktop; skeletons match menu rows

actions.label: Add to order
actions.outcome: Item enters the order and the count updates
actions.recovery: The item can be removed from the order

components.responsive: Button stays at the bottom on phones without covering the last item

actions.label: Order for 8:30
actions.recovery: Pending stays inside the button; failure preserves selection and allows retry

checks.scenario: Delay the fixture by 2 seconds: menu-shaped skeleton, stable replacement, and timeout error with retry
Add items, submit, trigger fixture failure, and retry; selection is preserved
Swap to another bakery and run the squint test on 360/1440 screenshots; record resulting changes
Video at 25% speed: button press, stamp and count roll, stable skeleton/menu crossfade, local pending; rapid Add clicks without queuing; reduced motion retains feedback without movement
